# UTS Service: full reference

Commercial locksmith, access control, door repair and automatic doors for apartment buildings and businesses across the Greater Toronto Area and southern Ontario.

## Who we work for
Property managers, condo boards, landlords, retail and franchise operators, offices and public sector buildings. Not individual homeowners.

## Services

### Locksmith
UTS Service is a commercial locksmith based in North York. We rekey and replace locks, build master key systems, install high-security cylinders and handle lockouts for apartment buildings, condos, stores, offices and public buildings across the GTA.

- Rekeying: New pins, new keys. The old keys stop working and the hardware stays.
- Master key systems: One key for the manager, separate keys for each unit or department.
- High-security locks: Cylinders that resist picking and drilling, with keys that can't be copied at a kiosk.
- Lock replacement: Worn or damaged locks swapped for commercial-grade hardware.
- Lockouts: Locked out of a unit, office or storefront? We get you back in.
- Key replacement: Lost keys replaced. When it makes sense, the lock is rekeyed so the lost key is useless.

Questions:
- Q: What is a master key system?
  A: A master key system lets one key open many locks while every other key opens only its own door. A property manager or superintendent carries the master. Tenants, staff or departments each get a key that works on their door and nothing else.
- Q: Should I rekey a lock or replace it?
  A: Rekey when the lock works fine but you no longer trust who has keys. The pins are changed so old keys stop working, and it costs less than new hardware. Replace the lock when it is worn, damaged, or you want a higher security grade.
- Q: What makes a lock high-security?
  A: A high-security cylinder is built to resist picking, drilling and forced entry. Most also use restricted keys, which can only be copied with the owner's authorization, so you know how many keys exist.
- Q: Can you rekey a whole building?
  A: Yes. We rekey single units at move-out and entire buildings after a change of management, a lost master key or a break-in.

### Access control
Access control replaces keys with credentials you can switch on and off: fobs, cards, PIN codes or fingerprints. UTS Service designs, installs and manages these systems for apartment buildings and businesses across the GTA, and takes over systems another company installed.

- Fob and card systems: The standard for apartment buildings and offices. Tap to enter.
- Keypads and PIN entry: Codes for staff doors, storerooms and shared spaces.
- Biometric readers: Fingerprint entry for rooms where a shared code is not enough.
- Fob management: We add, cancel and audit credentials for you, the same day.
- System takeovers: Inherited a system nobody understands? We sort out what you have and run it.
- Entry records: See which credential opened which door, and when.

Questions:
- Q: What happens when a fob is lost?
  A: The lost fob is cancelled in the system and stops working right away. Nobody needs to rekey a lock or hand out new keys. A replacement fob is issued to the person who lost it.
- Q: Fob, keypad or biometric: which is right for my building?
  A: Fobs and cards suit most apartment buildings and offices because each one belongs to a person and can be cancelled alone. Keypads suit low-risk shared doors. Biometric readers suit rooms where you need to be sure of the person, not just the credential.
- Q: Does access control keep a record of who came in?
  A: Yes. Most systems log each entry with the credential used, the door and the time. That record helps after an incident and shows which fobs are still in use.
- Q: Can you take over our existing fob system?
  A: Usually, yes. We'll look at what you have, tell you if it can be managed or should be replaced, and give you the price before any work starts.
- Q: What happens to the doors if the power goes out?
  A: It depends on how each door is set up. Some locks release when power is lost so people can always get out, and others stay locked from the outside. Battery backup keeps readers working through short outages. We set this up door by door.

### Door repair
Most door problems come from four parts: the closer, the hinges, the strike and the frame. UTS Service repairs and replaces all of them on commercial, storefront and apartment building doors across the GTA, so the door closes, latches and locks every time.

- Door closers: Adjusted or replaced so the door shuts firmly without slamming.
- Hinges and pivots: Sagging doors rehung on hardware rated for the traffic.
- Strikes and latches: Realigned so the door latches without a pull.
- Frames and alignment: Bent or shifted frames corrected so the door sits square.
- Panic bars and exit hardware: Exit devices repaired so people can always get out.
- Door replacement: When a door is past repair, we replace it and its hardware.

Questions:
- Q: Why won't my door latch?
  A: A door that will not latch usually has a closer that needs adjusting, hinges that have sagged, or a strike plate that no longer lines up with the latch. All three can be fixed without replacing the door.
- Q: Should a commercial door be repaired or replaced?
  A: Repair it when the door itself is sound and the problem is hardware: closer, hinges, strike or lock. Replace it when the door or frame is bent, rusted through or cracked, because new hardware on a damaged door will fail again.
- Q: What does a door closer do?
  A: A door closer is the arm at the top of the door that pulls it shut at a controlled speed. Set properly, it closes and latches the door without slamming. A leaking or worn closer is the most common reason a door slams or stays open.
- Q: Why does it matter if a fire door latches?
  A: A fire-rated door only does its job when it closes and latches by itself. If it is propped open, or the closer or latch has failed, it should be repaired promptly.

### Automatic doors
UTS Service installs, repairs and maintains automatic doors for commercial properties and apartment buildings across the GTA. That covers sliding doors, swing door operators and push-button openers that make an entrance easier for everyone to use.

- Sliding automatic doors: For lobbies and storefronts with steady foot traffic.
- Swing door operators: A motor added to a regular door so it opens by itself.
- Push-button openers: The accessible entrance button, installed and wired.
- Sensors and safety checks: Sensors tested so doors open for people and never close on them.
- Repairs: Doors that stick, shudder or stop are diagnosed and fixed.
- Scheduled maintenance: Regular visits that catch wear before the door fails.

Questions:
- Q: Can an existing door be made automatic?
  A: Often, yes. A swing door operator can be fitted to many existing doors, with a push button or sensor to trigger it. We check the door, frame and power supply first to confirm it will work.
- Q: Sliding or swing: which automatic door do I need?
  A: Sliding doors suit wide entrances with constant traffic, like lobbies and storefronts. Swing operators suit a single existing door, and cost less because the door and frame stay.
- Q: Do automatic doors need regular service?
  A: Yes. Sensors, motors and safety features wear with use. Regular checks keep the door safe and catch problems before the entrance goes out of service.
- Q: Do push-button openers help with accessibility?
  A: Yes. A power operator with a push button is a common way to make an entrance barrier-free, which many Ontario buildings are required to provide. We install hardware that meets the code requirements for your building.

### Building Program
One account for every lock, reader and door across a portfolio of buildings: fob management, master key systems, scheduled checks and a priority line.

## Building types

### Apartments and condos
UTS Service looks after the entrances of apartment and condo buildings across the GTA: fob and intercom systems, lobby and automatic doors, garage entrances, unit rekeys at move-out, and master key systems for property managers and condo boards.
- Q: Do you work with condo boards and superintendents?
  A: Yes. We work with property managers, condo boards and on-site superintendents, and keep one record of the locks, keys and fobs for each building.
- Q: Can you rekey a unit between tenants?
  A: Yes. Rekeying at move-out means the last tenant’s keys no longer work, and it costs less than replacing the lock.
- Q: What happens when a resident loses a fob?
  A: The lost fob is cancelled in the system right away and a new one is issued. Nothing else in the building has to change.

### Retail and franchise
UTS Service keeps storefront doors and locks working for retailers and franchise operators across the GTA. We repair and replace storefront locks, closers and panic bars, rekey after staff changes, and apply the same hardware standard at every location.
- Q: Can you look after all of our locations?
  A: Yes. One account covers every store, with the same team and the same hardware standard at each site.
- Q: A manager left with keys. What should we do?
  A: Rekey the locks they had keys for. It is quick, costs less than new locks, and with restricted keys you control who can make copies from then on.

### Offices and corporate
UTS Service sets up and manages access for offices across the GTA: card and fob entry by floor or department, master key systems for the rooms that still use keys, and entry records that show who came in and when.
- Q: Can access be limited by floor or department?
  A: Yes. Each card or fob is set to open only the doors that person needs, and that can be changed at any time without touching the hardware.
- Q: What happens when an employee leaves?
  A: Their card or fob is switched off in the system. If they also held keys, the affected locks are rekeyed.

### Public sector
UTS Service installs and maintains locks, access control and automatic doors in public buildings across the GTA. We use code-compliant hardware, keep entrances accessible, and work around the people who use the building every day.
- Q: Is your work code compliant?
  A: Yes. We install hardware that meets fire code and accessibility requirements, and we'll tell you if something you have doesn't.
- Q: Can you work while the building is open?
  A: Yes. We plan the work so entrances stay usable and secure while the building is occupied.

## Service areas

### Toronto
Cities and towns: Toronto, North York, Scarborough, Etobicoke.
Toronto runs on towers, storefronts and lobbies. Rental and condo high-rises need fob systems that keep up with move-ins and move-outs. Downtown and midtown offices need card access by floor. Main-street shops and mall units need storefront locks and closers that survive thousands of openings a week.

### Peel Region
Cities and towns: Brampton, Mississauga, Caledon.
Peel mixes dense condo towers in Mississauga with warehouses and industrial units around Pearson and plazas across Brampton and Caledon. Heavy doors, shipping areas and shared entrances take a beating, and multi-unit buildings need tight control over who has keys and fobs.

### York Region
Cities and towns: Vaughan, Markham, Richmond Hill, Aurora, Newmarket, East Gwillimbury, Georgina, King, Whitchurch-Stouffville.
York Region has some of the newest buildings in the GTA: condo towers and townhouse communities in Vaughan, Markham and Richmond Hill, business parks along Highway 7 and the 404, and plazas in every town up to Georgina. New buildings still need their access systems managed and their doors kept adjusted as they settle.

### Durham Region
Cities and towns: Pickering, Ajax, Whitby, Oshawa, Clarington, Uxbridge, Scugog, Brock.
Durham covers lakeshore cities like Pickering, Ajax, Whitby and Oshawa and rural townships up to Brock. Rental apartment buildings, plazas, schools, offices and municipal buildings all depend on entrances that lock, open and close the way they should.

### Halton Region
Cities and towns: Burlington, Oakville, Milton, Halton Hills.
Halton runs from lakeside condos and offices in Oakville and Burlington to fast-growing Milton and the industrial parks of Halton Hills. Busy entrances, office suites and shared buildings all need locks, readers and doors that one team keeps track of.

### Beyond the GTA
Cities and towns: Hamilton, Barrie, Guelph, Cambridge, Kitchener, Waterloo, St. Catharines, Niagara Falls, Brantford.
Beyond the GTA we mostly work for property managers and brands with several sites, such as franchise locations, retail chains and buildings in a portfolio, who want one team and one standard across every location in Hamilton, Niagara, Kitchener-Waterloo, Guelph, Brantford and Barrie.
